text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Decision on lifting Yugoslav sanctions will not be made today but the political climate for this is ripe and the decision is only a matter of days, according to the Politka New York correspondent.
- Yugoslav parliamentary delegation, headed by Lower House Speaker Radoman Bozovic leaves today on a three-day visit to Sofia.
- Yugoslavia and Austria start third round of talks in Vienna on an inter-state social security convention.
- Yugoslavia's chief representative in Croatia Veljko Knezevic says he hopes Belgrade and Zagreb will soon abolish visas following the example of European countries.

- Belgrade department stores Robne Kuce Beograd DD to renew long-term export-import deals with China, initially importing $5 million worth of goods, and later to import this amount every three months.
- Representatives of nine Danube river countries to meet in Belgrade from September 26 to 29.
- Yugoslavia has 566,375 refugees of whom over 60 percent wish to remain in the country, according to figures of a recent refugee census.
- Workers of Kragujevac arms factory decide to "freeze" strike if they receive their outstanding holiday pay today.
- Credibility of OSCE is in question over disputed ballots in some municipalities, says acting Vice President of Bosnian Serb Republic Biljana Plavsic.
- Serbian minister for private enterprise Radoje Djukic criticised the federal and republican governments for stifling the private sector with high taxes.
- Yugoslavia to continue talks with London Club of creditors at the end of the month in Belgrade, says John Eisenhammer, spokesman for Lowe Bell Financial.
- Economic situation in Kosovo is improving and the political situation is stabilising according to Socialist Party of Serbia officials who visited Kosovo province.
- Yugoslav arms manufacturers to attend Athens arms fair from October 1-5, for the first time after introduction of sanctions.

- Sanctions against Yugoslavia will soon be lifted and the country will return to international organisations. Only then can it be compared to other countries in transition, says economist Jurij Bajec
